extracted.intended_audience: financial reporting professionals, SEC registrants, accountants, and transaction teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on US SEC filing and financial‑reporting requirements when a registrant acquires, disposes of, or is probable to acquire a business, including Rule 3-05, Article 11 pro forma requirements, significance tests, period/age rules, and special scenarios (foreign acquirees, real estate, investment funds, troubled institutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-acquisition financial statements (S-X Rule 3-05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-acquisition financial statements of the acquiree (often called ‘Rule 3-05 financial statements’) are required when an acquisition is significant under Regulation S‑X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which pre-acquisition financial statements are required and how they must be prepared depends on many factors including the acquisition’s significance, whether the acquiree is domestic or foreign, whether carve-out statements are available, and the filing mechanism. The Handbook explains both the 'periods' question (how many periods) and the 'age' question (how old the statements can be) when applying Rule 3-05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma financial information (S-X Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information is required under S‑X Article 11 when an acquisition or disposition is significant or otherwise triggers pro forma disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pro forma requirements are a separate set of requirements from Rule 3-05 and may overlap. The Handbook explains when pro forma information is required (including for dispositions) but notes that detailed presentation rules for pro forma information are outside its scope in some sections; however, registrants must follow Article 11 when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting mechanisms (Form 8-K, registration statements, proxy statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3-05 financial statements and pro forma information are provided through Form 8-K, registration statements, and proxy statements, with timing and inclusion rules varying by mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 8-K must generally be filed within four business days of the transaction, but there can be a grace period for furnishing Rule 3-05 financial statements and pro forma information. If a registration statement becomes effective or proxy materials are mailed during that grace period, financial statements/pro forma may have to be included in the registration/proxy. Probable acquisitions may be reported on registration or proxy statements even if not on Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance determination using Reg S-X Rule 1-02(w) tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance of an acquisition, disposition, or probable acquisition is determined using three tests: the investment (purchase price) test, the income test (with pretax income and revenue components), and the asset test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each test produces a percentage (ratio). The test with the highest percentage determines significance. For the income test, two component tests are computed and the lower of the two is the income test result. Examples and worked ratios are provided in the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test components (pretax income and revenue)
rubrics_metrics.description: The income test comprises two component tests: registrant’s share of the acquiree’s pretax income divided by the registrant’s consolidated pretax income; and registrant’s share of the acquiree’s consolidated total revenue divided by the registrant’s consolidated total revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lower of the two component results is the income test result. The Handbook provides guidance on computing registrant’s share and how to treat consolidated amounts when multiple parties are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highest-test-wins rule for significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The significance of a transaction equals the highest percentage result from the investment, income, and asset tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if investment=28%, income=32%, asset=42%, significance = 42%. That highest-test determines filing obligations and period requirements under Rule 3-05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance thresholds and filing triggers (>20%, >40%, >50%, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different significance thresholds trigger different filing and disclosure obligations (e.g., >20% significance generally triggers Form 8-K and Rule 3-05 implications; other thresholds affect number of periods required and aggregation rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook summarizes thresholds: acquisitions >20% significant normally require Rule 3-05 statements; the number of annual periods required varies by significance (does not exceed 20% = none; exceeds 20% but not 40% = one fiscal year; exceeds 40% = two fiscal years). Aggregation thresholds (e.g., >50% aggregate when filing registration/proxy) and timing-based thresholds (e.g., 74-day/75+ day distinctions) affect what must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related acquisitions treated as a single transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisitions are related and treated as a single transaction for significance testing if there was common control or common management of the acquired businesses, or the acquisitions were conditioned on a single common event or on the acquisition of another business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related acquisitions aggregated may push a registrant over filing or period thresholds. The Handbook explains examples of relatedness and how to apply the single-transaction treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrelated acquisitions tested individually, with aggregation for registration/proxy filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Unrelated acquisitions are tested individually for significance, but individually insignificant acquisitions may be aggregated for filings of registration statements or certain proxy materials to determine whether aggregate significance exceeds thresholds (e.g., >50%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If aggregate significance >50% for acquisitions since the registrant’s most recent audited balance sheet, pro forma information (and in some cases financial statements) for the aggregate may be required even though each acquisition was individually insignificant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods question: number of annual and interim periods required
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of audited annual and unaudited interim financial statement periods required for the acquiree depends on the acquisition’s level of significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary table: does not exceed 20% → none; exceeds 20% but not 40% → one fiscal year audited; exceeds 40% → two fiscal years audited and interim requirements (e.g., most recent unaudited interim period and comparative interim when applicable). Special circumstances may change these requirements (see section 4.2.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age question: age of financial statements and the 'specific date' concept
rubrics_metrics.description: The acceptable age of Rule 3-05 financial statements depends on the filing type and a 'specific date' associated with that filing (Form 8-K initial filing date; registration statement effective date; proxy mailing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 'specific date' falls 'shortly after' the acquiree’s most recently completed fiscal year, prior fiscal year may suffice. The meaning of 'shortly after' varies by filing type (Form 8-K, registration, proxy) and filer status; guidance and tables explain the applicable day thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Shortly after' timing thresholds by filer type
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Shortly after' for Form 8-K depends on filer status: large accelerated filer = no more than 59 days after fiscal year end; accelerated filer = no more than 74 days; non-accelerated (including nonpublic) = no more than 89 days. For registration statements and proxy materials, 'shortly after' = within 45 days after fiscal year end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specific date falls within these thresholds, relief to use the prior fiscal year’s statements may be available; additional relief under Rule 3-01(c) may apply when specific dates fall outside 45 days for registration/proxy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim financials age rule (135/130 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim period financial statements of the acquired business are required if the required annual period financial statements are dated 135 days or more before the filing date of the Form 8-K, effective date of a registration statement, or mailing date of proxy material; for large accelerated and accelerated filers this threshold is 130 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interim statements are provided, they must be dated fewer than 135 (or 130) days before the relevant filing date. Timing diagrams and examples (A/B/C scenarios) illustrate when particular interim periods are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-4/F-4 and merger proxy registration statement specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms such as S‑4/F‑4 (and related proxy statements) contain specific requirements for information about the business being acquired, including financial information, which are distinct from S‑X Rule 3-05 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although similar in some respects, S‑4/F‑4 requirements may differ (e.g., form-specific disclosures). The Handbook summarizes typical filing requirements based on type of business combination (cash merger, stock merger, tender offer, exchange) and consideration (cash vs securities). See chapter 5 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'business' for SEC reporting (continuity of operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether assets acquired constitute a 'business' under SEC rules is based on SEC’s definition in Regulation S‑X, focusing on whether there is continuity of operations before and after the transaction (which differs from FASB Topic 805’s definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only acquisitions of 'businesses' trigger Rule 3-05; asset acquisitions follow a different set of reporting requirements. The Handbook discusses factors to consider when assessing continuity of operations and examples where a transaction is not a business acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisitions of foreign entities: basis and conversion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3-05 requirements also apply to acquisitions of foreign entities by domestic registrants and acquisitions by foreign private issuers, but the basis for preparation (GAAP) and certain age rules may differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If acquiree’s statements are in different GAAP, amounts are converted to the registrant's GAAP. Foreign acquiree statements may be prepared under US GAAP, IFRS as issued by the IASB, or home country GAAP reconciled to IFRS/US GAAP depending on whether the acquiree meets the definition of a foreign business or would qualify as an FPI; age requirements for foreign business acquirees may follow Item 8 of Form 20‑F instead of S-X Rule 3-01/3-02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial registration statements: special Rule 3-05 departures and put‑together transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: When an entity becomes a registrant via an initial registration statement, certain portions of Rule 3-05 cannot be applied because the registrant has not previously been a registrant; timing, significance evaluation, and put‑together aggregation rules differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate acquisitions since the earliest year for which the registrant’s own audited financial statements are required. Rule 3-05 financial statements can sometimes be omitted if operations have been included in the registrant’s post-acquisition results long enough. Put‑together transactions (shell acquiring multiple businesses) treat all acquired businesses as related for significance testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAB 80 election evaluation for initial registration statements
rubrics_metrics.description: SAB Topic 80 provides an election to provide different information than required by S‑X Rule 3-05 for companies filing an initial registration statement, subject to meeting certain criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook notes that prior to 2021 SAB 80 was relief but after 2021 it might not be more advantageous than applying Rule 3-05. Registrants should evaluate whether SAB 80 or Rule 3-05 yields better outcomes given the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real estate acquisitions scoped to Rule 3-14 when qualifying
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquired set of assets and activities is in the scope of S‑X Rule 3-14 (real estate) rather than Rule 3-05 if it (1) meets the SEC’s definition of a business and (2) substantially all the revenues it generates are through leasing of real property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For qualifying real estate operations, significance is determined using only the investment test. If significant (>20%), registrant can file abbreviated financial statements (audited statement of revenues and certain expenses) rather than full Rule 3-05 financial statements. The Handbook provides comparison tables and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating 'substantially all' revenues from leasing — qualification guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as a real estate operation under Rule 3-14, the acquired business must generate substantially all revenues through leasing of real property; businesses with more variable operations (hotels, nursing homes, auto dealerships, etc.) generally do not qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of qualifying operations include shopping centers and malls. Non-qualifying examples (more susceptible to short-term cost/revenue variations) include hotels, motels, nursing homes, golf courses, auto dealerships, and equipment rental operations. The Handbook explains the economic rationale (continuity/predictability of leasing cash flows).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of abbreviated financial statements for real estate acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When Rule 3-14 applies and abbreviated financial statements are permitted, historical abbreviated financials include an audited statement of revenues and certain expenses; many typical financial statements (e.g., statement of cash flows) are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenses not expected to be comparable to future operations may be excluded (mortgage interest, leasehold rental, depreciation, amortization, corporate overhead, income taxes). Pro forma financial information per Article 11 and specific disclosure/supplemental requirements also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6-11 applies to registered investment companies and business development companies
rubrics_metrics.description: S‑X Rule 6-11 (not Rule 3-05) applies when certain investment funds acquire other investment funds or when such acquisitions are probable; registrants subject to Rule 6-11 include registered investment companies and BDCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Rule 6-11: the asset test does not apply and modified versions of the investment and income tests apply. The Handbook provides a decision tree to determine whether financial statements and supplemental information are required, including whether securities are being registered for the holders of the target fund and aggregate significance tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated financial statements/ carve‑out statements eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that acquires less than substantially all the assets and liabilities of an entity may provide abbreviated or carve-out financial statements of the acquired business instead of full financial statements, if certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision tree: if company acquired less than substantially all and separate full financial statements for the acquired business are not available, consider whether carve-out statements can be provided; if carve-outs are available, provide audited carve-out statements per Rule 3-05; if not, full audited financial statements of the acquired business are required. The Handbook details carve-out preparation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubled financial institutions — when Rule 3-05 statements may be omitted or waived
rubrics_metrics.description: For 'troubled financial institutions' (in receivership/conservatorship/operating under federal supervision, controlled by a federal regulator, or acquired in a federally assisted transaction), audited Rule 3-05 financial statements may not be reasonably available and may be omitted in some circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff may waive Rule 3-05 audited statements for troubled institutions if audited statements are not reasonably available and total acquired assets do not exceed 20% of the registrant’s assets; waivers may be considered in more significant cases depending on federal assistance. Where waived, registrant should provide other disclosures (audited statement of assets acquired and liabilities assumed if available, unaudited statements of operations/cash flows where reasonably available, narrative quantified discussion of anticipated effects, disclosure of federal assistance terms, and Industry Guide 3 information where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission due to lack of continuity of operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements of an acquired entity need not be provided under Rule 3-05 if continuity of operations is substantially lacking such that historical financial information is not material to understanding future operations (SEC Rule 11-01 considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant must persuasively demonstrate lack of continuity and include a representation in the filing; even when omitted, applicable descriptive disclosures, pro forma information, and other transaction information should be furnished to the extent reasonably available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put-back arrangements and extension for audited statements
rubrics_metrics.description: If assets conveyed in a transaction are subject to rights allowing the registrant to put the assets back to the seller upon due diligence completion, an extension for filing audited statements may be available under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than 25% of acquired assets may be put and the put period does not exceed 120 days, registrant should timely file an unaudited statement of assets acquired and liabilities assumed with full disclosure of put terms; within 21 days after the put period lapses, file an audited statement unless effects are already reflected in an existing audited balance sheet. Some offerings under the Securities Act may be prevented until audited statements are filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures when historical audited financials are waived or omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: When audited financial statements required by Rule 3-05 are waived or omitted (e.g., troubled institution waiver or lack of continuity), the staff expects alternative financial and narrative disclosures to compensate for the omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected disclosures include: audited statement of assets acquired & liabilities assumed (if required), unaudited statements of operations and cash flows where reasonably available, quantified narrative discussion of anticipated effects on financial condition/liquidity/capital/resources/operating results, disclosures about federal assistance and its likely effects, amounts of acquired loans/investments (fair value, principal, yields), and an explanation of the basis for omission of historical financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable acquisitions: reporting when probability threshold crossed
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential acquisitions are not subject to the standard Form 8-K reporting requirements unless they cross the SEC probability threshold for being 'probable'; however, probable significant acquisitions may need to be reported on registration or proxy statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registrant should determine whether an unconsummated acquisition is probable and then test significance; 'very' significant probable acquisitions may be individually reported even pre‑consummation. The Handbook explains considerations and examples for probability determinations.
